target_profile.system_boundary: The hashicorp/raft Go library snapshot (module github.com/hashicorp/raft, commit c0dc6a0b). One Raft instance (Raft) with its main state thread (run/runFollower/runCandidate/runLeader), a follower-replication goroutine per peer, an FSM apply goroutine, a snapshot goroutine, and pluggable LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore/Transport. Not in scope: the embedding application FSM semantics, wire framing internals, and the operators' deployment process.
protocol_contexts: Leader election and term/authority management over a fixed or changing voter set
Log replication from a single elected leader to followers with commit-index propagation
One-at-a-time cluster membership change with Staging/Nonvoter/voter suffrage
Pre-vote campaign (default enabled) that probes electability without incrementing the term
Leadership transfer by pre-replication plus a TimeoutNow RPC
Snapshot install and log replay for recovery/resynchronization
external_interfaces: Public Raft API (Apply, Barrier, VerifyLeader, AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer, LeadershipTransfer, Snapshot, RecoverCluster)
ownership: All protocol state transitions and configuration state are owned by the main state thread; follower-replication goroutines only touch per-peer replication state and report matches into the shared commitment struct under its mutex.
selection_injection: Transport and stores are caller-injected; pre-vote is auto-disabled when the injected Transport does not implement WithPreVote (api.go NewRaft).
variants: protocolVersion < 2 uses legacy LogAddPeerDeprecated/LogRemovePeerDeprecated configuration entries and encodePeers
Single-voter configurations take hot paths (verifyLeader quorumSize==1)
PreVoteDisabled / transport not supporting pre-vote falls back to a direct election
unknowns: Net/TCP transport framing and its reordering guarantees were not read in this turn.
File/in-memory snapshot stores and the fuzzy/ or bench/ packages were not read.

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement: elect a leader and extend/commit the replicated log.
activities.realization_summary: A candidate runs a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that does not change its term and, on winning it, a real campaign (electSelf) that increments and persists the term and asks voters for a vote. Followers decide the vote in requestVote/requestPreVote with leader-stickiness, log up-to-date and one-vote-per-term guards. The elected leader dispatches a no-op for its term, replicates to each peer (followerReplication), and advances the commit index through the commitment struct once a quorum's matchIndex reaches at least the first entry of the leader's own term.
variants: pre-vote disabled falls back to electSelf directly
unknowns: Behaviour of the pipeline replication fast path under partial responses was only skimmed.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority: term ownership, state transitions, and leadership transfer.
activities.realization_summary: Authority is the persisted current term plus the per-term vote. setCurrentTerm persists the term before exposing it; setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term observed in a vote request or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update. leadershipTransfer pre-replicates to the target then sends TimeoutNow; the target sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer and runs an election without pre-vote, and the flag is reset after each candidate run.
variants: candidateFromLeadershipTransfer bypasses both pre-vote and appendEntries step-down for equal terms
unknowns: Authority effects of leadership transfer when the target never wins were not fully traced.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation.
activities.realization_summary: Each follower-replication goroutine keeps a nextIndex, backs off on failures, walks nextIndex down when a peer rejects an AppendEntries, and falls back to sending the latest snapshot when the needed log entry is gone. handleStaleTerm stops replication and asks the main thread to step down when a peer reports a newer term.
unknowns: sendLatestSnapshot/InstallSnapshot handling and its interaction with concurrent truncation were not fully read.

activities.realization_summary: Configuration changes are appended as log entries computed by nextConfiguration from the latest configuration (with an optional prevIndex guard) and are in effect as soon as appended: appendConfigurationEntry updates the latest configuration and the leader's commitment set immediately, then startStopReplication adds/removes peers. A new change may only be accepted once latestIndex==committedIndex and the leader has committed an entry in its term.
variants: protocolVersion<2 emits legacy peer log entries
unknowns: Interplay of an in-flight config change with leadership transfer was not traced.

activities.realization_summary: processLogs feeds committed entries to the FSM via fsmMutateCh in batches of MaxAppendEntries, advancing lastApplied, and responds to the corresponding log futures; it panics if a committed log entry cannot be read.
unknowns: runFSM goroutine body was not read in this turn.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support.
activities.realization_summary: NewRaft restores the newest snapshot, then replays the log after the snapshot index to rebuild the latest/committed configurations; the newest configuration log entry also drives committed/latest updates during normal AppendEntries processing. Snapshot metadata carries the configuration and its index.
variants: snapshot.Version>0 uses stored configuration; older snapshots decode peers
unknowns: Snapshot lifecycle goroutine (runSnapshots) and file_snapshot.go were not read.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion.
activities.realization_summary: Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier enqueue a logFuture on applyCh with an optional enqueue timeout; VerifyLeader enqueues a verifyFuture; both block on the future and are answered by the main thread. A nonzero timeout only bounds the enqueue, not the completion.
unknowns: Completion/cleanup of blocked futures on step-down and shutdown was not fully traced.

behaviors.execution_owner: commitment struct, written by leader and follower-replication goroutines, consumed by Raft.main
behaviors.trigger: a local log write or a successful AppendEntries reply calls commitment.match; recalculate notifies commitCh
legal_preconditions: matchIndexes only contains voters of the configuration passed to newCommitment/setConfiguration
implementation_guards: match only increases a server's stored index
commitIndex advances only if the quorum index is > commitIndex AND >= startIndex (the first index of the leader's term)
important_branches: setConfiguration immediately switches the matchIndexes/quorum to the newly appended configuration (documented as in effect at append time)

writes: setCommittedConfiguration when latestIndex is now committed
stepDown if the leader is no longer a voter
important_branches: removing the leader from the configuration sets stepDown and either shuts down or transitions to follower after the group is applied

behaviors.trigger: an election, a newer-term RPC, or a state change
implementation_guards: setCurrentTerm persists before exposing the term and panics if persistence fails
setState clears the known leader on every transition
durable_effects: current term is durable before it becomes authoritative

legal_preconditions: target is a voter with replication state; otherwise the future errors
implementation_guards: only one transfer at a time (leadershipTransferInProgress)
replicates to the target until nextIndex exceeds lastIndex before sending TimeoutNow
transfer flag is reset after each candidate run

at most one uncommitted configuration

nextIndex is decremented toward resp.LastLog+1 on rejection
switches to pipeline mode when healthy

steps down when contacted < quorumSize

an optional timeout only bounds enqueue (ErrEnqueueTimeout), not completion

behaviors.trigger: processLogs sends a batch of commitTuple to fsmMutateCh
implementation_guards: applyBatch is selected whenever the FSM implements BatchingFSM; applySingle is used only when it does not
writes: FSM state via Apply / ApplyBatch / StoreConfiguration
important_branches: non-batching path: LogConfiguration calls configStore.StoreConfiguration(index, DecodeConfiguration(data)) only when the FSM implements ConfigurationStore, and LogConfiguration without ConfigurationStore returns early without advancing lastIndex/lastTerm

batching path: LogConfiguration is appended to sendLogs and passed to ApplyBatch; applySingle (and therefore StoreConfiguration) is never invoked, and lastIndex/lastTerm advance to the batch's last entry regardless of type

for a FSM implementing both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore this batching branch is the observed behaviour: a committed LogConfiguration entry reached only ApplyBatch while StoreConfiguration was never called (execution a898e056 of direct check d37a13c5)
async_boundaries: futures are responded after the batch is applied
unknowns: Whether a FSM implementing both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore is a supported configuration, i.e. which interface is expected to own configuration persistence, is not stated by either doc comment; the delivery gap itself is now an observed violation of the ConfigurationStore contract (confirmed in execution a898e056).

behaviors.execution_owner: Transport connection goroutine via the installed handler (net_transport heartbeatFn -> Raft.processHeartbeat -> appendEntries)
behaviors.protocol_context: peer sends a pure AppendEntries heartbeat: Term != 0, leader address present, PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm zero, no entries, LeaderCommitIndex zero
behaviors.trigger: net_transport classifies the decoded AppendEntries request as a heartbeat and calls the handler installed at api.go:616
legal_preconditions: every other entry into appendEntries first passes checkRPCHeader, which rejects an RPC header outside the supported protocol-version window
implementation_guards: no checkRPCHeader call on this path: the handler invokes appendEntries directly
the remaining AppendEntries work is naturally empty because the previous-log, entry and commit fields are zero

observed on a goroutine-free node (execution 198781118): the fast path acted on an out-of-window pure heartbeat (term 0 -> 5, sender adopted as known leader, last contact refreshed), while the identical request was rejected with ErrUnsupportedProtocol and changed nothing on the normal path (execution event normal_path_heartbeat_result)
important_branches: only pure heartbeats take this route, so log matching and commit propagation are not performed here; the effects are state/term/leader/last-contact updates

the route exists only for a Transport that actually invokes the callback: net_transport does (S43), while InmemTransport.SetHeartbeatHandler is a documented no-op, so in-process transport tests never exercise this path (S45); the library's own integration test demonstrates the callback contract by calling r.processHeartbeat(rpc) from inside a custom handler (S44)
async_boundaries: runs on the transport connection goroutine concurrently with the Raft main thread; the fields it touches are individually lock- or atomic-protected
unknowns: Whether a peer outside the supported protocol-version window can deliver a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment, and whether the missing guard is deliberate design, are unresolved; that the fast path does not apply the guard is now an observed violation of claim-heartbeat-header-gate, not a hypothesis.

behaviors.protocol_context: any state; an incoming TimeoutNow RPC from a peer whose RPC header passes the version window
legal_preconditions: none stated in the handler beyond the RPC-header version window applied by processRPC
implementation_guards: no term is available on the request (TimeoutNowRequest carries only an RPCHeader)
no membership, voter or known-leader check is performed

observed (execution 554a0abc): a TimeoutNow whose sender is absent from the receiver's two-voter configuration was honoured exactly like one from a configured voter - leader cleared, state Follower -> Candidate, privilege false -> true, no error - while the out-of-window control was rejected with ErrUnsupportedProtocol, so the version window is the only guard on this path
important_branches: the handler responds success unconditionally after clearing the leader context
async_boundaries: the receiver then runs runCandidate on the main thread, which reads the transfer flag
unknowns: Whether a peer outside the receiver's configuration can reach this handler in a real deployment (the observation uses a fabricated identifier), and whether leaving it unguarded is deliberate design, remain unresolved; that the handler grants the privilege to such a sender is now an observed violation of claim-timeout-now-attribution.

behaviors.execution_owner: raftState accessors (getLastIndex/getLastEntry) fed by NewRaft, restoreSnapshot and every log write
behaviors.protocol_context: startup and steady state; the log may be empty while a newer snapshot exists
behaviors.trigger: any read of the node's last index/entry, e.g. building RequestVote, dispatching a new log entry, or serving AppendEntries
legal_preconditions: the snapshot index/term is set when a snapshot is restored or taken
implementation_guards: getLastIndex returns max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex)
getLastEntry returns the snapshot's pair when the snapshot is newer than the log
writes: lastLog via setLastLog on every local log write and on AppendEntries
lastSnapshot via setLastSnapshot on snapshot restore/take
important_branches: a node restarted with an empty log but a snapshot at index N therefore advertises and resumes at N rather than at 0, so no log index below the snapshot is reused

facts.meaning: The server's persisted current term and, for that term, the single candidate it has voted for (possibly itself).
facts.validity_context: A term value is authoritative once persisted by setCurrentTerm; a stored vote is only consulted for the term it was cast (lastVoteTerm == req.Term).
facts.durability: Written through StableStore before being used; persistence failure for the term panics, for a vote the request is rejected.
facts.recovery: Read at NewRaft time into currentTerm and reused by the duplicate-requestVote check.

facts.meaning: The leader's commitIndex: the highest index the leader holds to be committed because a quorum of voters store a matching log.
facts.validity_context: Only meaningful for the term in which the leader is elected; advancing it requires the quorum match to be at least startIndex (the first entry of the leader's own term).
facts.durability: Not durable on the leader; recomputed from match indexes; followers persist the same entries the leader has and learn the index from LeaderCommitIndex.
facts.recovery: Recomputed from replication after an election; no persisted commit index is trusted on restart.

facts.meaning: Per-server record that a server's durable log agrees with the leader through at least a given index.
facts.validity_context: Derived from a successful local write or a successful AppendEntries reply (last entry index), and only tracked for voters of the configuration currently installed in the commitment struct.
facts.recovery: Re-derived after a leader election as replication catches up.

facts.meaning: The cluster configuration currently in effect (latest) and the configuration known to be committed, each with its log index.
facts.validity_context: latest is in effect from the moment its log entry is appended; committed is the newest configuration whose entry has been committed. At most one uncommitted configuration exists at a time.
facts.durability: Persisted as log entries and in snapshot metadata.
facts.recovery: Rebuilt at startup by restoring the snapshot and replaying configuration log entries.

facts.meaning: The election campaign state: votes granted/refused in a pre-vote campaign and votes granted in a real campaign, for a specific proposed term.
facts.validity_context: Only valid within one runCandidate invocation; a newer term observed in any response forces a step-down.
facts.recovery: Restarted from scratch after an election timeout.
unknowns: No distinct consumer Behavior is mapped in this partial map; the tally is consumed inline by the runCandidate select loop.

facts.meaning: The application FSM's own durable record of committed cluster configuration entries, as delivered by the library.

identity.key: committed configuration log entries delivered to the FSM

facts.validity_context: The library is the only party that can deliver a committed configuration entry to the FSM, via ConfigurationStore.StoreConfiguration on the non-batching path or by sending a LogConfiguration to ApplyBatch on the batching path.
facts.durability: FSM-defined; configuration.go documents this as making the persistent FSM state behave as a complete snapshot recoverable without an external snapshot.
facts.recovery: FSM-defined; the interface exists precisely so that recovery need not depend on an external snapshot.
unknowns: Whether implementing both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore is a supported combination, and therefore which written contract governs configuration persistence for batching FSMs, remains unresolved; the absence of the StoreConfiguration call path for such a FSM is observed, not inferred.

facts.meaning: The privilege held by a receiver of a TimeoutNow request to skip the pre-vote campaign and to send votes that peers grant even though they already have a leader.
facts.validity_context: Set by timeoutNow on receipt of any TimeoutNow request that passes the RPC-header version window, and cleared after each runCandidate invocation; it is the only stated protection against reuse.
facts.durability: In-memory only; not persisted, so a restart loses it.
facts.recovery: No recovery; a restarted node starts without the privilege.
unknowns: The privilege is granted for any in-window TimeoutNow request, including one whose sender the receiver's configuration does not contain (observed, execution 554a0abc); whether that reachability is real and whether the design intends to trust leader discipline remain open.

facts.meaning: The node's position in stable storage: the last log entry it holds together with the last snapshot it holds, and the effective last index/term derived from the two.
facts.validity_context: The effective last position is max(log, snapshot); the snapshot pair wins when the snapshot index exceeds the log index, which is the normal state after log compaction or a restart with an emptied log.
facts.durability: The log entries and the snapshot are durable; the cached pair is recomputed at startup (lastLog from LogStore.LastIndex, lastSnapshot from the restored snapshot).
facts.recovery: NewRaft reads the log's last index, restoreSnapshot sets lastApplied and the last snapshot, and restoreSnapshot does not need to rewrite lastLog because the accessors take the maximum.
unknowns: none recorded: the max-of-two accessors explain the empty-log-with-newer-snapshot case that would otherwise look like index reuse

surfaces.reason: Body (raft.go:1814+) was only skimmed; snapshot receive path and its configuration handling are unread.

Leader-side snapshot shipping (replication.go:299-386) was read after this Surface was saved: it lists snapshots, opens the newest, sends InstallSnapshot with the snapshot's configuration and index, records a match at meta.Index on success and handles a newer term via handleStaleTerm. What remains unread is the snapshot store implementations' ordering/persistence guarantees and the follower-side stream handling beyond the response, so the Surface stays deferred rather than claiming coverage.
FSM application goroutine (fsm.go:86-130) was located but not read.
Snapshot lifecycle (snapshot.go:72-120) was located but not read.
Manual recovery path (api.go:313-360) not read beyond its doc comment.
Wire framing and connection handling (net_transport.go:81-100) are transport infrastructure, not Raft responsibility.
Config validation and reload paths (config.go:333-360) not read.

Sourced discrepancy: ConfigurationStore documents StoreConfiguration is invoked for each committed configuration entry (configuration.go:44-52), but the only call site is in applySingle (fsm.go:118), which the batching dispatch never reaches (fsm.go:127-186). Investigated as Candidate claim-config-store-delivery.

Sourced discrepancy in the appendEntries entry paths: processRPC calls checkRPCHeader before dispatching AppendEntries (raft.go:1390-1413), but the heartbeat fast path processHeartbeat calls appendEntries directly with no read of checkRPCHeader (raft.go:1415-1436), and net_transport routes any pure AppendEntries heartbeat (Term != 0, leader addr present, no entries, no prev-log fields, LeaderCommitIndex 0) to that handler (net_transport.go:660-686, 724-733). An AppendEntries whose RPCHeader.ProtocolVersion is outside the supported window that checkRPCHeader rejects on the normal path would therefore still be accepted on the fast path, where appendEntries can step the receiver down, persist a newer term, set the sender as known leader and refresh lastContact. Whether the window outside the fast path's route is reachable with a legal peer and what consequence it has is not established.

Read while looking for a new lead (api.go:713-741, config.go:267-...): ReloadConfig stores the new configuration and notifies leaderNotifyCh/followerNotifyCh only when HeartbeatTimeout decreases, so a decreased LeaderLeaseTimeout is not signalled and the leader's current lease timer keeps the old value until it fires. Whether that delay has a consequence worth investigating was not established, and the other reloadable fields are read per iteration by their loops. Low consequence; recorded rather than escalated.

Sourced asymmetry found while reading the snapshot receive path: after a successful InstallSnapshot the handler updates lastApplied and lastSnapshot and then compacts (raft.go:1928-1953), but it never calls setLastLog, and its only setLastLog callers are NewRaft, liveBootstrap, restoreUserSnapshot, dispatchLogs and appendEntries. Its compaction removes entries only up to the installed snapshot index (snapshot.go:213-259, maxLog = min(snapIdx, lastLogIdx-trailing)), so any entries the follower already holds beyond that index survive. For a follower whose log is longer than the installed snapshot (a divergent branch), getLastEntry therefore keeps returning that tail's index/term until the next matching AppendEntries truncates it, even though the FSM state and committed configuration now come from the snapshot. Whether such a longer divergent branch is reachable and whether the window has a consequence (vote comparisons use getLastEntry) is not established.

formation.explanation: A follower whose heartbeat timer expires while it is an eligible voter transitions to Candidate and runCandidate starts a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that proposes currentTerm+1 without touching the term. Each other voter answers in requestPreVote with the leader-stickiness, membership and log-up-to-date guards and without persisting anything. If a quorum of pre-votes is granted the candidate runs electSelf, which persists the new term and a self-vote, then requests votes; voters persist the vote in requestVote subject to the same guards plus one-vote-per-term. The first tally to reach quorumSize() sets the candidate to Leader. The leader then appends a no-op for its term and replicates; the commitment struct advances commitIndex only when an actual quorum's matchIndex reaches at least startIndex, the first index of the leader's own term.

context.explanation: Authority is the durable current term plus the durable per-term vote; there is no global leader identity. setCurrentTerm persists a term before it is exposed and setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term seen in RequestVote or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update, so context is lost by observation, not by a clock. Leadership transfer pre-replicates to the target and sends TimeoutNow; the target marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer so that it skips pre-vote and is not stepped down by an equal-term AppendEntries from the outgoing leader, and the flag is cleared after the candidate run. The configuration context is the pair (latest, committed); latest is in effect from the moment its entry is appended.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet in three places. (1) Eligibility for formation is read from the configuration context: only voters of the latest configuration are asked for votes and only their match indexes count for commitment, and the commitment struct is rebuilt from the configuration at leader setup and at each configuration change. (2) The leader's advancement duty is gated by its term context: configurationChangeChIfStable is only non-nil once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (commitIndex >= startIndex), which is why a no-op is dispatched on election even with no client work. (3) Old work is bounded by present authority: a persisted vote is only honoured for its own term, an AppendEntries reply that reports a newer term drives handleStaleTerm and a step-down, a conflicting suffix truncation rolls latest back to committed, and on step-down the leader fails all inflight log futures with ErrLeadershipLost while replication goroutines are stopped.

open_details: appendEntries has an explicit TODO (raft.go:1541): if StoreLogs fails after a truncation, lastLog is left stale. Whether any real store can fail there, and its consequence, is unresolved.
electSelf returns a nil response channel when persisting the self-vote fails (raft.go:2023), leaving the candidate to wait out its election timer; this is a storage-failure path only.

checkLeaderLease assumes leaderState.replState contains every voter of the latest configuration (raft.go:1054); ordering on the main thread appears to guarantee this, but a nil-map lookup would panic and was not tested.

The pre-vote path treats a transport 'unexpected command' error as a granted pre-vote (raft.go:2084-2090), which is intentional for mixed versions but was not analysed for a genuinely unreachable peer.
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships are explained from read code and the membership design document, and the connection (configuration context gating formation, own-term commit gating configuration changes, and stale/old work being bounded by term and vote context) is sourced. Residual anomalies are local and recorded under open_details rather than blocking the overview.
